2609.25809.title: You Only Need 2/3 of the Chosen Experts: An Empirical Study of Dynamic Expert Pruning in Fine-Grained MoE LLMs
2609.25809.paper_summary: Fine-grained mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures have become a mainstream design for open-weight LLMs, with hundreds of experts and increasingly many selected per token. This shift makes dynamic expert pruning an attractive route to cheaper inference. Yet existing evidence comes largely from coarser architectures and likelihood-scored multiple-choice benchmarks, leaving three central questions open in the fine-grained regime: how redundant per-token expert selection is, how effectively existing pruning methods exploit that redundancy, and what governs a model's sensitivity to pruning. We fill this gap with a systematic empirical study of twelve fine-grained MoE checkpoints spanning nine architecture families, with a core suite of eleven benchmarks covering knowledge QA, mathematics, code generation, and general reasoning. We find that expert selection is far more redundant than the field's operating points assume: uniformly retaining about two thirds of the selected experts preserves 98.8% of unpruned performance on average, requiring only a one-integer change and delivering 1.2-1.7x measured speedup across two serving backends. This simple baseline leaves little room for dynamic allocation at conservative budgets: even the best published rules differ from it by under 1% at matched expert budgets. Their value emerges under aggressive pruning, where the best rules recover up to 3.0% over uniform truncation, with gains concentrated in the generative tasks that suffer the sharpest degradation. Sensitivity to aggressive pruning also depends on the model: larger and thinking models are more resilient, whereas multimodal models are more vulnerable. Together, these findings reveal how much expert computation fine-grained MoEs can dispense with, and establish when dynamic allocation earns its complexity, informing both practical deployment and future pruning methods.
2609.25809.paper_summary_zh: 細粒度的專家混合（MoE）架構已成為開放權重 LLM 的主流設計，擁有數百個專家，並且每個標記選擇的專家數量也在不斷增加。這一轉變使得動態專家修剪成為降低推理成本的有吸引力的途徑。然而，現有的證據主要來自較粗糙的架構和基於可能性的多選基準，留下了三個核心問題在細粒度範疇中尚未解決：每個標記的專家選擇有多冗餘、現有的修剪方法在多大程度上利用了這種冗餘，以及什麼因素決定模型對修剪的敏感性。我們通過對十二個細粒度 MoE 檢查點的系統實證研究填補了這一空白，這些檢查點涵蓋了九個架構系列，並且有一組核心的十一個基準，涵蓋知識問答、數學、代碼生成和一般推理。我們發現專家選擇的冗餘程度遠高於該領域的運作點假設：均勻保留約三分之二的選定專家平均能保留 98.8% 的未修剪性能，只需改變一個整數，並在兩個服務後端上實現 1.2-1.7 倍的測量加速。這一簡單的基準在保守預算下幾乎沒有動態分配的空間：即使是最好的已發表規則在匹配專家預算時也僅與其相差不到 1%。它們的價值在於激進修剪的情況下出現，最佳規則在均勻截斷上恢復了最多 3.0% 的性能，增益集中在遭受最劇烈降級的生成任務上。對激進修剪的敏感性也取決於模型：較大和思維能力較強的模型更具彈性，而多模態模型則更脆弱。綜合這些發現揭示了細粒度 MoE 可以省去多少專家計算，並確定了動態分配何時值得其複雜性，為實際部署和未來的修剪方法提供了指導。
